intended_object: The predicate that an L-subalgebra P of L ⊗_k R is stable under the semilinear Galois action of Gal(L/k), where σ acts by l ⊗ r ↦ σ(l) ⊗ r. This is the Galois-stability hypothesis of Galois descent for subalgebras (from the docstring and module documentation).
explanation: `coefficientwise σ` is `Algebra.TensorProduct.map σ id`, i.e. l ⊗ r ↦ σ(l) ⊗ r, which is the standard semilinear Galois action on L ⊗_k R. IsStable asks that every σ ∈ Aut_k(L) maps P into P. Because these maps form a group action, this is the same as each σ mapping P onto P, i.e. Galois-stability. The library uses it as the hypothesis of `baseChange_descended_eq` (a stable P is the base change of its preimage in R), which is exactly the descent statement. The section variables FiniteDimensional and IsGalois are not used in the body. Lean includes them automatically, but that is harmless: the notion is only meaningful in the finite Galois descent setting, and R is already an arbitrary commutative k-algebra. I am not aware of a Mathlib declaration for this action or for stability under it.
